subject: EdgeHealth private hosting: enclave discovery and next steps
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_c@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeHealth private hosting: discovery recap + asks

Hi Samira — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and the pragmatic next steps we agreed so your infra and security teams can evaluate private hosting (VPC vs on-prem appliance).

Key pain & goals you reiterated:
- Data residency: all patient PII must remain in your AWS account in us-east-1 and never egress to third-party networks.
- Regulatory driver: state-level health regulations + upcoming audit require evidence of key management and audit logs retention.
- Availability target: 99.9% for inference endpoints used by clinician workflows; burst scaling for daytime peak.

Technical constraints discussed:
- EdgeHealth prefers private IP peering (AWS PrivateLink / ENI) or on-prem appliance behind a dedicated NAT; public egress only via customer-controlled NAT & proxy.
- No inbound public IPs to model hosts; SSH/bastion for support only, with static allowlist and jumpbox auditing.
- HSM/KMS: customer-managed key material required for token encryption and at-rest model artifacts.
- Air-gap consideration: if required, a sealed appliance with manual update process (physical or SFTP transfer) is acceptable, but timeline and procurement lead time increase.

Immediate asks for your infra/security to confirm (items we need to proceed with a technical SOW/POC):
1) Which connectivity pattern do you prefer? (PrivateLink peering, Transit Gateway, or colo appliance behind dedicated NAT) — list pros/cons if you have one in mind.
2) Egress allowlist IPs and port ranges we should expect to need for control-plane health checks (we will provide a minimal set).
3) KMS/HSM integration method: KMS key ARN(s) or HSM vendor + certificate rotation policy.
4) Compliance evidence folder owner — who on your security team will own SOC2/SIEM log review?

Attached: quick network sketch and a checklist we use for VPC/on-prem qualification.

Proposed next steps & timeline:
- You: confirm connectivity pattern and point person for security by EOD Thu (3 business days).
- Us: produce a short technical SOW and a POC plan (2–3 workdays after your confirmation).
- Commercial: Ben will follow with a draft licensing/POC quote after SOW.

If it helps, we can run a 30‑minute deep-dive with your network engineer next week — Ben and Neha will join.

Thanks again,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
attachments: edgehealth-network-sketch.pdf (diagram), redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgehealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeHealth Security <security@edgehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_c@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 17:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeHealth private hosting: discovery recap + asks

Maya — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. Quick answers before I loop in our netsec lead (Aisha) and infra owner: 

1) Preferred connectivity: Transit Gateway peering into our us-east-1 account. We prefer centralizing egress through our perimeter proxies. Appliance is a fallback if latency for certain regions becomes an issue.
2) Expected egress: we will need the concrete IPs from you, but expect that our proxies will permit outbound TLS to a narrow set of control-plane endpoints only.
3) KMS: we'll use our AWS KMS (key ARN will be provided to support team). HSM is currently via vendor HSM for highest-sensitivity stores; we need to confirm whether Redwood can integrate with our PKCS#11 interface — Neha / Ben, can you confirm support?
4) Compliance owner: security@edgehealth.com will own evidence collection. They prefer pre-flight templates and an early copy of audit-relevant logs.

Timeline: we can confirm the connectivity pattern and contact owners by Thu EOD. We are aiming for a Q4 POC. Please include procurement timelines in the commercial quote.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, EdgeHealth
phone: +1 617-555-0167

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgehealth.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_c@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeHealth private hosting: discovery recap + asks

Hi Samira — quick technical clarifications from the infra/solutions side. Short answers and what we'll include in the SOW.

- Transit Gateway: supported. We'll provide recommended route tables and a minimal set of control-plane CIDRs for allowlisting. Control-plane checks include health pings and metrics egress (TLS) — ports 443 only.
- PrivateLink vs TGW: PrivateLink avoids asymmetric routing for tenant traffic but requires NLB setup. TGW is simpler for your centralized proxy pattern. We'll include both options in the SOW and call out latency/management tradeoffs.
- KMS / HSM: Redwood supports AWS KMS key usage via cross-account grants. For PKCS#11 HSMs, we require a small connector that runs in your VPC (we ship a signed container). If that model doesn't work, we can run an HSM-backed instance in your account under a customer-managed VM (details in SOW).
- Bastion support: we recommend an audited bastion with time-limited jump tokens; we can support key-based or OIDC jump with session recordings.

I'll attach a short checklist for the TGW flow and a recommended NAT/proxy diagram for your security team. Ben / Maya: once Samira confirms owners, I'll schedule a 30-minute tech dive with Aisha + their infra owner.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx (TGW checklist), tgw-proxy-diagram.png (sketch)

Samira — appreciate the quick turnaround. On commercial / timeline:

- We'll size a POC quote for 8 vCPU-equivalent inference capacity (approx 4–6 throughput units) and include two weeks of implementation/validation support.
- Procurement: typical lead time for an on-prem appliance procurement (if chosen) is 8–12 weeks; VPC-based POC can usually start within 2–3 weeks after SOW and account setup.
- I'll add an appendix to the SOW that outlines cancellation & rollback commitments and a small credit for early-stage POC sign-off (to make timelines work with your audit).

Next steps from our side: Maya and I will draft the SOW today; Neha will produce the technical appendix. Samira — if you can confirm the owners (Aisha + infra lead) by EOD Thu we will lock the call next week for the deep-dive.

Ben
